questions.text: What is the source-backed MDPE multiplier range per SPP 202 Sec 5.2?

options.text: 1.5-2.5 per SPP 202 Sec 5.2

questions.rationale: SPP Document 202, Section 5.2 states that the MDPE multiplier ranges from 1.5 to 2.5, depending on office setup, overhead, the Architect's experience, and project complexity. The article body explicitly warns not to treat 2.8, 3.0, or 3.5 as source-backed MDPE multipliers; 2.7-3.2 is an exam trap. Source: PRBoA SPP 202 Sec 5.2 (https://www.architectureboard.com.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/1.4-2010-SPP-for-PH-Architects.pdf).
questions.explanation: Understates for high-rise complexity; 1.8–2.0 is appropriate for straightforward projects. Understates for high-rise complexity; 2.0–2.3 is appropriate for straightforward to moderate projects. Overstates; 3.5–4.0 exceeds the typical Philippine practice range and may price the architect out of competitive bidding. Complex projects (high-rises, specialized facilities, institutional buildings) typically use multipliers of 2.7–3.2 in current Philippine architecture practice. Complex projects (high-rises, specialized facilities): multiplier = 2.7–3.2; significant regulatory, structural, or coordination complexity.

questions.text: An architect proposes MDPE with estimated DPE of PHP 3,000,000, using a source-backed multiplier of 2.0 (within the SPP 202 Sec 5.2 range of 1.5-2.5), resulting in a PHP 6,000,000 fee. The estimated PCC is PHP 150,000,000. What is the effective percentage, and how does this compare to a Group 3 percentage-of-PCC approach?

options.text: 4.0% effective; below Group 3's base rate, making MDPE more economical for the architect on this scope
4.0% effective; above Group 3's base rate, making percentage-of-PCC more favorable
6.0% effective; exceeds Group 3's base rate, making MDPE inappropriate
20% effective; excessive and inappropriate for any project group, indicating a calculation error

questions.rationale: Fee = DPE x M = PHP 3,000,000 x 2.0 = PHP 6,000,000. Effective percentage = 6,000,000 / 150,000,000 = 4.0%. The multiplier 2.0 is within the SPP 202 Sec 5.2 range of 1.5-2.5; 2.8 is not source-backed and must not be used. Source: SPP 202 Sec 5.2 (https://www.architectureboard.com.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/1.4-2010-SPP-for-PH-Architects.pdf).

questions.text: SPP 202 Sec 5.2 states the MDPE multiplier ranges from 1.5 to 2.5. Which statement about how the multiplier is broken down is source-backed?

options.text: SPP 202 gives only the total multiplier range of 1.5-2.5; it does not publish an overhead sub-range such as 1.4-1.7
SPP 202 fixes the overhead component at 1.4-1.7 of direct personnel cost
SPP 202 mandates a 0.30 profit add-on plus a 0.15 non-technical add-on
SPP 202 decomposes the multiplier into equal overhead and profit halves of 1.25 each

questions.rationale: SPP Document 202, Section 5.2 gives only the total multiplier range of 1.5-2.5, with qualitative factors (office setup, overhead, the Architect's experience, project complexity). It does not decompose the multiplier into an overhead sub-range of 1.4-1.7 or any other fixed sub-components; such decompositions are exam traps. Source: SPP 202 Sec 5.2 (https://www.architectureboard.com.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/1.4-2010-SPP-for-PH-Architects.pdf).
questions.explanation: Understates overhead; 1.0–1.2 would only represent 0–20% of DPE, insufficient for typical firm operations. Overstates overhead; 1.8–2.0 would represent 80–100% of DPE, beyond the typical 40–70% range. Significantly overstates; 2.0–2.5 would represent more than 100% of DPE, which is excessive for overhead alone. Typical overhead represents 40–70% of direct personnel cost in Filipino architecture firms, translating to an overhead multiplier component of 1.4–1.7. Overhead component = 1.4–1.7 (from 40–70% of DPE); emerging/lean firms use 1.3–1.4, large firms use 1.6–1.7.

questions.text: How should an architect select an MDPE multiplier for a project with innovative design and high regulatory complexity, per SPP 202 Sec 5.2?

options.text: Select a multiplier within the source-backed 1.5-2.5 range, moving higher for greater overhead, experience, or complexity; SPP 202 lists qualitative factors and does not publish add-on amounts
Add 0.1-0.3 for innovation and 0.1-0.2 for regulatory complexity to the base multiplier
Use a fixed multiplier of 2.8 for all innovative projects
Always use the lowest multiplier (1.5) regardless of complexity, to stay competitive

questions.rationale: SPP Document 202, Section 5.2 states the MDPE multiplier ranges from 1.5 to 2.5 and lists only qualitative factors (office setup, overhead, the Architect's experience, project complexity). It does NOT publish a +0.1-0.3 innovation adjustment, a +0.1-0.2 regulatory adjustment, or any fixed add-on schedule. Such add-ons are exam traps. Source: SPP 202 Sec 5.2 (https://www.architectureboard.com.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/1.4-2010-SPP-for-PH-Architects.pdf).

questions.text: A firm agrees an MDPE multiplier of 2.0 (within the SPP 202 Sec 5.2 range of 1.5-2.5) on a direct personnel cost of PHP 900,000. What is the Fee before reimbursables?

options.text: PHP 2,000,000 (from a 1.55 + 0.30 + 0.15 decomposition)

questions.rationale: SPP 202 Sec 5.2 gives the total multiplier range of 1.5-2.5 and does NOT decompose it into 1.55 overhead + 0.30 profit + 0.15 non-technical; that decomposition is an exam trap the article body rejects. Fee = DPE x M = PHP 900,000 x 2.0 = PHP 1,800,000 before reimbursables. Source: SPP 202 Sec 5.2 (https://www.architectureboard.com.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/1.4-2010-SPP-for-PH-Architects.pdf).
questions.explanation: Calculates only the overhead component (1.55), omitting profit and non-technical factors. Calculates 1.55 + 0.30 + 0.30 (incorrect profit calculation) = 2.15; misplaces non-technical factor. Overstates by 0.5; this may confuse percentage with different multiplier components or use incorrect arithmetic. Overhead: 55% = 1.55 multiplier component; Profit: 30% = 0.30 component; Non-technical: 15% = 0.15 component. Total = 1.55 + 0.30 + 0.15 = 2.0. Multiplier decomposition: overhead 1.55 + profit 0.30 + non-technical 0.15 = 2.0; typical for straightforward to moderate projects.

questions.text: Which statement is source-safe about MDPE and creative design?

options.text: MDPE is source-limited to non-creative work because creative design value cannot be measured merely by time spent
MDPE is mandatory for all creative design work
Creative design is excluded from professional service value
Creative design is always paid as contractor profit

rationale.a: SPP 202 says MDPE applies to non-creative work and does not account for creative work because design value cannot be measured by time spent.
rationale.b: The checked source says MDPE does not account for creative work.
rationale.c: The source does not devalue creative design.
rationale.d: Contractor profit is unrelated to this Architect compensation method.
rationale.correct: SPP 202 says MDPE applies to non-creative work and does not account for creative work because design value cannot be measured by time spent.
rationale.takeaway: This limitation explains why MDPE is not universal.

questions.text: Per SPP 202 Sec 5.2, how is the MDPE multiplier M defined?

options.text: M is the multiplier to account for overhead and reasonable profit, ranging from 1.5 to 2.5
M is a three-component framework of overhead, profit, and non-technical factors
M is the reimbursable expense added after the fee
M is a fixed statutory multiplier of 3.0 for all projects

questions.rationale: SPP Document 202, Section 5.2 defines M as the multiplier used to account for overhead and reasonable profit, with a source-backed range of 1.5 to 2.5 and qualitative factors (office setup, overhead, Architect's experience, project complexity). SPP 202 does NOT define a three-component (overhead + profit + non-technical) framework; that framework is an exam trap. Source: SPP 202 Sec 5.2 (https://www.architectureboard.com.ph/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/1.4-2010-SPP-for-PH-Architects.pdf).
